note: BROU only, among the main banks: Itaú Uruguay's manual of rates and prices (version 1 October 2026) prices its cards' yearly charge in indexed units but states no card interest rate, so its cards can't be written; Santander Uruguay's site sits behind Incapsula and BBVA Uruguay's refused the request (403). Banco República's particular conditions for its Visa credit cards (conditions in force February 2025), read in full: the Internacional, Oro and Platino cards, each with its yearly charge with VAT (billed in three monthly instalments; issue costs nothing). The Internacional's charge is waived in full on average spending of 35,000 pesos a month the year before, written as 420,000 in the year, and the Platino's on 60,000 a month, written as 720,000 (the 50% discounts on lower averages are steps not written; the Oro's table gives only a half discount up to 35,000, not written). Balances and cash advances in pesos bear an effective 65.00% a year, and late balances the moratory 84.38%, written as the penalty rate. Purchases abroad on the Internacional carry 3% plus VAT (whose rate isn't stated), written as 3%; the Oro and Platino are exempt. Cash advances at BROU's own branches and network cost nothing. No grace period is stated; the minimum payment is below. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) added OCA, the country's largest card issuer (a card company of the Itaú group, regulated by the Banco Central del Uruguay): its current rates and charges (in force from 1 October 2026), read in full, for the OCA card and the OCA Visa Internacional and Internacional Oro: balances in pesos bear an effective 61% a year and cash advances 80%, and late balances 70%, written as the penalty rate (the sheet says VAT at the basic rate is added to its figures, a rate it doesn't state, so none is added); the card's service costs 130 indexed units a quarter (162.50 on the Oro), VAT included, written in pesos at the indexed unit's value on 1 October 2026, 6.6516 pesos (the INE's series), as 864.71 and 1,080.89; the OCA card is free for its first year (the card's own page), written as the fee waived for its first four quarters (the page doesn't say the Visa cards share it, so their fee isn't waived); the late-payment fine under Law 18.212, art. 19, 50 indexed units, is written as a late fee of 332.58 pesos; using the card abroad costs 2.44%, VAT included; a cash advance in Uruguay costs nothing. The 50-unit fine for paying in full within 48 hours after the due date isn't written. No minimum payment or grace period is stated. Tried and not used: Créditos Directos' Tarjeta D states its rates without a period (133% plus VAT, not said to be yearly), so it isn't written; Creditel's site sits behind Incapsula; Scotiabank Uruguay's and Anda's home pages answered but weren't searched for a tariff in this pass; HSBC Uruguay's, Banco Heritage's and the Banco Central del Uruguay's didn't answer. Minimum payments (wave 5, 30 October 2026): BROU's particular conditions, read again, state it: the interest, fees and taxes, any overdraft, and 10% of the whole balance owed, written for its three cards as 10% with the interest on top (fees, taxes and the over-limit amount not modelled). No minimum payment is published for OCA's cards; tried: OCA's rates and charges in force from 1 October 2026 (it says only that amounts over the limit are included in full in the minimum), its credit card page (no figure; archive.org's availability API names a snapshot of 11 September 2026, not readable from here, and none of the rates sheet); no rule of the Banco Central del Uruguay setting a share was found in the documents read, and no search was made for one in this wave.
